Pebble Spring looked at the first blueprint with wide, curious eyes. The lines were straight, which was unlike anything in the forest. He picked up his staff and tapped it against the ground. A small pulse of green energy rippled outward. The dirt softened just enough to accept the first foundation stone. His friends watched from the sidelines, cheering softly. One by one, the stones began to settle into place. It was slower than expected, but steady. By noon, the base of the wall was visible. Pebble Spring felt a surge of pride in his chest. However, the wind picked up suddenly, swirling leaves around them. He shielded his face and continued working. The next day brought rain, which made the mud slippery. Several stones slipped out of alignment during the storm. He had to use more magic to coax them back. The effort left him feeling drained and thirsty. He drank deeply from the nearby spring water. The taste was crisp and cold, refreshing his spirit. When he returned to the site, the sun was setting. The shadows stretched long across the unfinished structure. He realized how much more work still remained. Yet, he did not feel discouraged by the task ahead. Instead, he saw each challenge as a lesson in patience. As the days turned into weeks, the group found themselves dealing with various minor inconveniences, such as leaking roofs, stuck doors, and strange noises coming from the walls, all of which contributed to a spotty record of progress that worried the leader deeply.
